_README: Human adjudications that settle a queued ruling. The other half of rejections.json:
that file records 'do not publish', this one records 'a person read this and it is
fine'. Without it the review queue cannot shrink -- verify.py re-surfaces every
medium-confidence and flagged item on every run, so the same items get re-read forever
and the queue stops meaning anything.
An approval is scoped to the exact text and sources it was given. `signature` is
verify.py's fingerprint of (ruling text + cited comment ids + thread context) at review
time; if any of those change the approval lapses and the item returns to the queue. So
an approval cannot silence a ruling that was later rewritten, which is the whole risk of
Write `signature: null` to approve regardless of future edits. Do that only for a
finding about the *source* rather than the ruling -- e.g. 'this answer is terse because
the question carried the polarity, and that is correct here'.
approved   the ruling is faithful and well-sourced; the model's objection is wrong or moot
accepted   the objection is fair but the ruling is the best available; reason says why
A ruling that should change is not recorded here -- change it. A ruling that should go
is not recorded here either -- that is rejections.json.
